claim_verdicts.evidence: deployment/web.md: "This generates the app, including the assets, and places the files into the `/build/web` directory of the project." The stage-3 build (DonHang.App/build/web) holds main.dart.js; its flutter_bootstrap.js buildConfig reads "builds":[{"compileTarget":"dart2js","renderer":"canvaskit","mainJsPath":"main.dart.js"}].

The browser fetches none of build/web/canvaskit from app-web. The build's flutter_bootstrap.js: `n.canvasKitBaseUrl?n.canvasKitBaseUrl:e.engineRevision&&!e.useLocalCanvasKit?W("https://www.gstatic.com/flutter-canvaskit",e.engineRevision):"canvaskit"`; buildConfig has engineRevision, no useLocalCanvasKit. flutter_tools 3.47.2: `web-resources-cdn` defaultsTo: true; useLocalCanvasKit = !useCdn. up.sh runs plain `flutter build web`. The variant choice and the .symbols part are right.

(True as written only once scripts/up.sh builds with `--no-web-resources-cdn`; see issue on section 3.)

claim_verdicts.evidence: Inspection of the stage-3 build: the only compiled Dart output is main.dart.js (no part files; the other .js are flutter.js, flutter_bootstrap.js, flutter_service_worker.js and canvaskit/*.js engine loaders), and buildConfig names one build with mainJsPath main.dart.js. faq.md: "If you import a huge Dart library but only use a self-contained two-line method, then you only pay the cost of the two-line method".

build-modes.md, release for web: "The build is minified and tree shaking has been performed." deployment/web.md: "the compiler reduces the size of the compiled code by removing unused code (known as _tree shaking_)"; table row release: Yes / Yes. faq.md: "you only pay the cost of the two-line method".

flutter_tools 3.47.2 build_web.dart:26 `addTreeShakeIconsFlag();`, flag 'tree-shake-icons' defaultsTo kIconTreeShakerEnabledDefault (= true, build_info.dart:24), help "Tree shake icon fonts so that only glyphs used by the application remain."; applied when buildMode.isPrecompiled. Build output: assets/fonts/MaterialIcons-Regular.otf is 8396 bytes. Release notes 3.10: "tree shake icons from web builds".

The captured output (outputs/stage-3/scripts/frontend/web-bundle.txt) masks every number as `...`, and running gzip on build/web/main.dart.js (3,032,853 bytes raw) was not permitted in this session, so the gzip/raw ratio could not be observed. The script itself (lines 19-23) does compute `gzip -c -9 | wc -c` next to the raw size, as stated.

RFC 9110 §12.5.3: "When sent by a user agent in a request, Accept-Encoding indicates the content codings acceptable in a response." §8.4: "The \"Content-Encoding\" header field indicates what content codings have been applied to the representation ... and thus what decoding mechanisms have to be applied in order to obtain data in the media type referenced by the Content-Type header field."

Round 2, page reached. encode: "If omitted, `zstd` (preferred) and `gzip` are enabled by default." "the encoding is chosen based the request's Accept-Encoding header." minimum_length "(default: 512)"; default match lists Content-Type text/*, JavaScript, JSON, fonts, SVG, so not every response is packed. The page says nothing about a request with no Accept-Encoding; RFC 9110 §12.5.3 says absence means any coding is acceptable, so that part stays unsupported.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: `encode` with no options turns on zstd and gzip; Caddy picks one from the formats the browser lists in `Accept-Encoding`, for text-like responses such as `main.dart.js`. The files on disk stay as they are.

claim_verdicts.evidence: deploy/app-web/Caddyfile @ stage-3 lines 20-21: `encode` then `file_server`; @ stage-2 the same block has only `try_files {path} /index.html` and `file_server`. Captured output of web-bundle.sh @ stage-3: "GET http://localhost:8081/main.dart.js with Accept-Encoding: gzip" / "Content-Encoding: gzip".

Captured output lists 6 canvaskit/*.wasm, main.dart.js, canvaskit/wimp.js.symbols. ls -lS of build/web confirms the order (canvaskit.wasm 7284602 > chromium 5428806 > skwasm_heavy 5216217 > webparagraph 3729129 > skwasm 3593715 > wimp.wasm 3581677 > main.dart.js 3032853 > wimp.js.symbols 1813030). Script line 24 sums every file. There are six .symbols files, not one.

scripts/up.sh @ stage-3 line 12: `(cd DonHang.App && flutter build web >/dev/null)`; line 22 prints `app (web)   http://localhost:8081/`. docker-compose.yml @ stage-3, service app-web: image caddy:2.10.0, volume ./DonHang.App/build/web:/srv/app:ro, ports "8081:8081".

Opinion; supportable only with its condition. faq.md: tree shaking means "you only pay the cost" of the code used, so a package may add little or a lot; the measurement is what decides. Section 5 already states it conditionally; summary line 5 drops the condition.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: Every package in `pubspec.yaml` can add code to `main.dart.js`; running `web-bundle.sh` before and after adding one shows how much it added.

claim_verdicts.evidence: No docs sentence states it. The build's flutter_bootstrap.js loads the renderer (`l.renderer==="canvaskit"?d.canvasKit=I(d,r,f,h)`) and the entrypoint before the app runs, so main.dart.js and one engine build must arrive before any frame. "Every file the app needs" is too broad: initialization.md says fallback fonts are downloaded "when bundled fonts lack required glyphs", i.e. on demand.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: `main.dart.js` and the engine build must arrive before the first frame on any connection; a fast link shortens that wait, it does not remove it, and a first visit has no saved copy to start from.
